question: If I’m tracking a federal regulatory proposal, what’s the difference between looking in Part I and Part II of the Canada Gazette?
generated_answer:
The Canada Gazette is divided into three parts: Part I, Part II, and Part III. Part I contains official government notices, orders, and regulations. Part II contains proposed regulations, which are open for public comment. Part III contains regulations that are no longer open for comment. If you’re tracking a federal regulatory proposal, you should look in Part II of the Canada Gazette, as this is where proposed regulations are published for public comment. Once a regulation is finalized, it will be published in Part III of the Canada Gazette. 

For more information, you can refer to the Government of Canada's guide to the Canada Gazette: [https://www.canada.ca/en/canadian-heritage/services/canada-gazette.html](https://www.canada.ca/en/canadian-heritage/services/canada-gazette.html) 

If you're looking for a specific regulatory proposal, you can search the Canada Gazette database: [https://www.gazette.gc.ca/](https://www.gazette.gc.ca/) 

Please note that the Canada Gazette is only one source of information on federal regulatory proposals. You may also want to check the Government of Canada's Regulatory Registry, which provides information on current and upcoming regulatory proposals: [https://www.canada.ca/en/treasury-board-secretariat/services/regulatory-registry.html](https://www.canada.ca/en/treasury-board-secretariat/services/regulatory-registry.html) 

Additionally, you can also check the website of the relevant federal department or agency, as they may provide more detailed information on specific regulatory proposals.
